config.title: Enums & Tuples — Structured Constants

intro.title: Enums & Tuples — Structured Constants
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple program to manage a library's book status system. You'll learn how to use TypeScript enums to define a fixed set of constants, like 'Available', 'Borrowed', and 'Reserved', for tracking books. You'll also use tuples to store structured data, such as pairing a book's title with its publication year in a specific order. By the end, you'll understand how enums provide clarity and tuples enforce structure in your code.
intro.usecase: Enums and tuples are essential for creating structured, type-safe constants in real-world applications. For example, in a dashboard application, you might use an enum to define user roles like ADMIN, EDITOR, and VIEWER, ensuring only valid roles are assigned. Tuples are perfect for representing fixed data structures like coordinate pairs [x, y] in mapping interfaces or status codes with messages like [404, 'Not Found'] in API responses. These patterns prevent bugs by catching invalid values at compile time rather than runtime.

objectives: Implement a numeric enum to represent a set of related constants
Construct a string enum with custom values for improved readability
Initialize a tuple with fixed types and length for structured data
Manipulate tuple elements through indexing and type-safe assignment
Apply enums in conditional logic to control program flow
Integrate enums and tuples within function parameters and return types
Configure computed and constant members within enum declarations

steps.title: Import TypeScript and React
steps.instruction: Import React from 'react' to enable JSX and TypeScript for type checking in this lesson.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring React into your file. This is required for writing JSX in TypeScript.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a library for use
import React from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The file will have React imported, setting up the TypeScript environment with React for the lesson.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing React from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import React from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Define a numeric enum for user roles
steps.instruction: Define a numeric enum called UserRole with ADMIN, EDITOR, and VIEWER members. Place it above the App component.
steps.hint: Use the enum keyword followed by the name and curly braces containing the member names.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a UserRole enum with three members that can be used as structured constants.
successCriteria: A numeric enum named UserRole is defined with ADMIN, EDITOR, and VIEWER members.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a numeric enum with exactly ADMIN, EDITOR, and VIEWER members.
steps.feedbackWrong: The enum definition is missing or incorrect. Remember to use the enum keyword with the specified members.

steps.title: Define a string enum for status codes
steps.instruction: Define a string enum named Status with three members: PENDING, SUCCESS, and ERROR. Assign each a string value matching its name (e.g., PENDING = 'PENDING'). Place this enum definition above the App component.
steps.hint: Use the enum keyword followed by the name Status and curly braces. Inside, list each member with an equals sign and a string literal.
steps.expectedOutcome: A string enum named Status with PENDING, SUCCESS, and ERROR members is defined, each assigned a string value.
successCriteria: The Status enum is defined with three members, each assigned a string literal matching its name.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but ensure the Status enum has exactly three members (PENDING, SUCCESS, ERROR) and each is assigned a string value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the syntax: use 'enum Status { ... }' with each member assigned a string like PENDING = 'PENDING'.

steps.title: Create a tuple type for user data
steps.instruction: In your code, above the App component, create a tuple type alias named UserData that specifies the fixed order [string, number, boolean].
steps.hint: Use the 'type' keyword to define a type alias. The syntax for a tuple type is [Type1, Type2, Type3].
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: a tuple type for coordinates
type Coordinates = [number, number];
steps.expectedOutcome: A new type alias UserData is defined, representing a fixed-length array where the first element is a string, the second is a number, and the third is a boolean.
successCriteria: The UserData type alias is created with the correct tuple syntax: [string, number, boolean].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your type alias uses the exact tuple syntax [string, number, boolean] and is named UserData.
steps.feedbackWrong: use the 'type' keyword to create a type alias named UserData with the tuple type [string, number, boolean].

steps.instruction: Inside your App component, declare a variable named 'currentRole' and assign it the value UserRole.Admin from your numeric enum.
steps.hint: Use const to declare the variable and assign it the enum value using dot notation.

steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a variable that holds the Admin role value from your UserRole enum, ready to be used in your component.
successCriteria: A variable named 'currentRole' is declared and assigned the value UserRole.Admin.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the correct enum name and value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The variable wasn't declared correctly. Check the enum name and assignment syntax.

steps.title: Create a function to demonstrate enum usage
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, create a function named getRoleDescription that takes a parameter of type UserRole and returns a descriptive string based on the role value.
steps.hint: Define a function that uses a switch statement or if-else to return different strings for different UserRole enum values.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named getRoleDescription is defined inside the App component that accepts a UserRole parameter and returns a string.
successCriteria: The getRoleDescription function is created with proper TypeScript typing for its parameter and return type.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it accepts a UserRole parameter and returns a string description.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function wasn't created correctly. Check that you defined getRoleDescription inside the App component with proper parameter typing.

steps.title: Create a function to demonstrate tuple usage
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, create a function named formatUserData that takes a parameter of type UserData (the tuple type you defined earlier) and returns a formatted string describing the user.
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts a UserData tuple as its parameter and uses template literals to return a string combining the tuple's elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named formatUserData is added to the App component that accepts a UserData tuple parameter and returns a formatted string.
successCriteria: The formatUserData function is defined inside the App component, takes a UserData tuple parameter, and returns a string using template literals.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function accepts a UserData tuple parameter and returns a formatted string using template literals.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function formatUserData should be defined inside the App component, accept a UserData tuple parameter, and return a formatted string.

steps.title: Build the component markup structure
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, create a container div with a class of 'container' and add two sections inside it: one for displaying enum examples and another for tuple examples.
steps.hint: Add a <div className='container'> inside the existing outer div, then create two <section> elements within it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a structured layout with designated areas for enum and tuple content.
successCriteria: A div with className='container' is added, containing two section elements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you have a div with className='container' and two section elements inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The structure doesn't match what's needed. Check that you have a container div with two sections.

steps.title: Display enum and tuple values in the UI
steps.instruction: Inside the container's two sections, display the currentRole value, getRoleDescription output, and formatUserData output using JSX expressions.
steps.hint: Use curly braces {} to embed JavaScript expressions in JSX. Call your functions and reference variables directly.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying values in JSX

Current role: {currentRole}

Description: {getRoleDescription(currentRole)}

User data: {formatUserData()}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show the numeric enum value, its description, and the formatted tuple data in separate sections.
successCriteria: The JSX includes expressions that display currentRole, call getRoleDescription with currentRole, and call formatUserData.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're displaying all three values: currentRole, getRoleDescription(currentRole), and formatUserData() in the appropriate sections.
steps.feedbackWrong: The UI doesn't show the expected values. Check that you're using curly braces {} to embed the expressions and calling the functions correctly.
